title: Shape transitions and rare reversals in the elephant random walk
author: Arjun Pemmasani
abstract: At every superdiffusive memory, the initial biases for which the elephant random walk's limit density is bimodal form one open interval centred at $1/2$. Outside it, the density is unimodal with a unique local maximum. The proof controls first differences, their boundary histories and the dominant half of each finite count law; every finite law has at most two modal plateaus. For a fair first step, the density has two inflection points when unimodal and four when bimodal. A certified computation proves a unique modal transition at $a_*=0.6688128600146\ldots$, enclosed in an interval shorter than $3.3\cdot10^{-15}$, with the critical density unimodal. Bimodality for $a\ge4/5$ also has a proof without computation. As $a\to1$, a two-component Landau approximation holds uniformly over the initial bias, in total variation and scaled uniform density distance. It determines the locations and heights of the fair-start peaks. For rare reversals, an explicit total variation approximation by a truncated Luria--Delbr\"uck law gives a Landau local limit theorem with a rate. When $\log N\le x=N\varepsilon\le2\log N$, every mode lies at distance $x\log x+\lambda_{\mathrm L}x+O(\sqrt{x\log x})$ from an end. For even $N$, the origin and each end are equally likely at a unique reversal probability, with $N\varepsilon=2\log N-\log\log N-\log16+o(1)$. At this crossing, every even $N\ge8$ has two symmetric modal intervals and a unique interior minimum, by finite certified computations and analytic bounds.
